title: Penguins that give pebbles
hook: Some penguins build nests out of stones, and pick out pebbles for a mate.
peek: Gentoo and Adelie penguins build their nests from small stones. A male may bring a chosen pebble to a partner, and good stones are so prized that neighbours often steal them.
lede: Gentoo and Adelie penguins breed on rocky coasts around Antarctica, where there are no twigs to build with. Instead, they make nests from small stones piled into a low ring. A male will collect pebbles, and he may present one to his mate. It is easy to call this a proposal, but the stones are mostly practical building material for a shared nest.

bullets.text: When snow melts in the brief summer, the ground floods. A raised ring of stones keeps the eggs above the icy water, and nests with more stones tend to stay drier.

bullets.opening: A pebble presented to a mate
bullets.text: In courtship, a male may drop a stone at a female's feet. If she accepts, it goes into the nest. Both partners then keep adding stones throughout the season.
Good stones are in short supply, so penguins often sneak pebbles from nearby nests when the owners look away. Some stones probably change hands many times in a season.
Online posts often say a penguin searches the whole beach for one perfect pebble and mates for life. Many pairs do reunite, but the pebble is one of many, and partners sometimes change.
